exposure: Sleep duration trajectories during pregnancy (short-decreasing, medium-decreasing, long-increasing)
outcome: Factors associated with sleep duration trajectories
Impact of sleep duration trajectories on pregnancy and birth outcomes (assisted delivery, cesarean section, instrumental delivery, postpartum depression, premature birth, birth-weight-z-score)
cohort: 200 women from a mother-child cohort recruited from the French general population
finding: Three distinct sleep duration trajectories were identified during pregnancy, with older age and working beyond 28 weeks of gestation associated with shorter sleep durations, and these trajectories were linked to adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, including assisted delivery, postpartum depression, and lower birth weight.
mod_finding: Women with the short-decreasing sleep trajectory had a higher prevalence of cesarean section compared to the other groups.
